title: Sell Mineral Rights in Dacono, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Dacono, CO
metaDescription: Dacono sits in core southern Weld County Wattenberg acreage. See how nearby Niobrara-Codell horizontal units shape what your mineral or royalty interest is worth.
heroLead: Dacono is a small city in southern Weld County sitting well inside the productive core of the Wattenberg Field, close enough to Denver's northern suburbs to have grown steadily while remaining surrounded by active DJ Basin acreage.
intro: Operators have drilled extensively throughout this part of Weld County using multi-well horizontal pads targeting the Niobrara and Codell formations, and the area's mix of continued agricultural land and expanding residential development means both older vertical wells and recent horizontal units can be found within a few miles of each other.

sections.heading: Growth meeting an active drilling base
paragraphs: As Dacono's residential footprint has expanded, some new subdivisions sit near or over existing units, which brings local setback rules into play the way it does across the broader Front Range under SB 19-181. Existing production isn't affected by new setback rules, but where new pads get sited going forward is driven by them.

sections.heading: A strong candidate for active unit membership
paragraphs: Given how thoroughly this part of Weld County has been developed, a Dacono-area mineral interest has a genuinely good chance of sitting inside a current production unit, even if you've never received a royalty check because the interest was only recently pooled or because payment records went to a previous owner's address.

sections.heading: What we check before quoting
paragraphs: We confirm your legal description against current unit boundaries, pull operator-of-record and permit filings from the state, and build a decline curve from actual royalty statements where the interest has produced. Dacono-area interests span a wide range of values depending on exact position, so we don't quote off a flat area-wide number.

sections.heading: A note on older leases still in force
paragraphs: Some Dacono-area leases were signed years before the current unit boundaries were established, and it's common for those older agreements to still be in force through held-by-production clauses once a well is turned in line anywhere within the pooled unit. If your family's original lease predates recent horizontal development nearby, that doesn't mean it's expired — it may simply be riding on a well drilled elsewhere in the same unit.

faqs.question: I've never received a royalty check — could my interest still be in a producing unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, this happens more than people expect, often because payment records went to a previous owner's address or the interest was only recently pooled. We check current unit status directly.

faqs.question: How does new residential growth around Dacono affect existing wells?
faqs.answer: Existing production isn't affected by new local setback rules; those mainly shape where new pads can be sited going forward.

faqs.question: Is this a strong area for mineral value generally?
faqs.answer: It's core Wattenberg acreage with a long history of active horizontal development, so the odds of meaningful value are generally better here than in most other parts of the state.

faqs.question: What's the fastest way to get an accurate number?
faqs.answer: Send your legal description and any royalty statements you have. We can typically return a preliminary range within a few business days.

faqs.question: My original lease is decades old — is it still valid?
faqs.answer: It can be, if the unit it's part of has an actively producing well anywhere within its boundaries. We check current production and unit status rather than assuming an old signing date means the lease has lapsed.
